identity.name: West Berlin
alt_names: American, British and French sectors of Berlin

land.text: the American, British and French sectors of Berlin, divided from the Soviet sector in 1945

predecessors.note: Greater Berlin lay inside the Soviet zone but was jointly occupied (Allied-occupied Germany page).

land.text: Berlin, where 'East and West Berlin formally reunited and joined the Federal Republic as a city-state' on 3 October 1990

successors.note: The Federal Republic (federal-republic-of-germany, Cliopatria 1950-1990) and the reunified Germany share the date; the eu-22-e dossier starts the reunified state in 1990.

capitals.name: West Berlin (Rathaus Schöneberg)
capitals.note: 'run by an elected Governing Mayor and Senate seated at Rathaus Schöneberg'; the Western Allies had to approve these officials. Coordinates are the town hall's, not on the page. The page says East Germany made East Berlin its capital and the Western Allies recognised it only as the seat of government.

correction.text: the three Western sectors of Berlin, 479.9 km2 in the 1989 infobox; 'about two million' people

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Natural Earth's Berlin covers all Berlin (the Soviet sector too), so the named region is larger than the infobox's 479.9 km2; at the grid's resolution the two cannot be separated, and the renderer should hatch the cell as occupied land (rule 4). The page gives one area for all 45 years; the Wall (13 August 1961) and the Four Power Agreement (September 1971) moved no border.

region.text: the American, British and French sectors of Berlin

ledger.note: 1945: the Western Allies take their sectors of Berlin. 'The Western Allies and the Soviet Union divided Berlin into sectors in 1945. The Western Allies held the American, British, and French sectors, and the Soviet sector became East Berlin.' The page gives the year, not the month; the Allied-occupied Germany page adds that Berlin lay in the Soviet zone but was jointly occupied and divided into four sectors.
1945: the American sector of Berlin. The page names the three Western sectors but no districts, so the region is the Western part of Berlin.

September 1948: West Berlin becomes a separate jurisdiction. 'East and West Berlin became formally separate jurisdictions in September 1948' after a communist putsch in the city government; the infobox dates the 'Soviet-backed coup' to November 1948, the body to September, and the page does not reconcile them.

October 1958: the French sector passes from the Fourth to the Fifth Republic. 'The Fourth Republic was dissolved on 5 October 1958' (French Fourth Republic page; its introduction gives 27 October 1946 to 4 October 1958). Hand-over pair added by the eu-22-x reviewer so the 1990 occupation_end names the Fifth Republic.

October 1958: the Fifth Republic holds the French sector from the new constitution (infobox: 'New constitution adopted: 4 October 1958') until 3 October 1990. Hand-over pair added by the eu-22-x reviewer.

3 October 1990: the American sector's occupation ends. 'West Berlin remained under military occupation until 3 October 1990, when East and West Berlin formally reunited and joined the Federal Republic as a city-state.'
3 October 1990: the British sector's occupation ends (same sentence).
3 October 1990: the French sector's occupation ends (same sentence). Counterpart is the Fifth Republic (the Fourth ended in October 1958; reviewer eu-22-x).

region.text: West Berlin, with East Berlin, as the city-state of Berlin in the reunified Germany

ledger.note: 3 October 1990: West Berlin and East Berlin are reunited and join the Federal Republic as a city-state. The Two Plus Four Treaty 'paved the way for German reunification and an end to Western Allied occupation of West Berlin'; its provisions tying Berlin to the Basic Law 'only took full effect on 3 October 1990'.

wars.name: Berlin Blockade
wars.outcome: The Soviets blockaded the Western sectors from 24 June 1948 to 12 May 1949; the Western Allies supplied the city by the Berlin Airlift and kept it; no border moved.
wars.note: A siege without a front; listed with empty zones. The Wall of 13 August 1961 to 9 November 1989 closed the sector border without changing it.

certainty.note: The sector boundary through the city was fixed by the occupation agreements and later walled (13 August 1961); the page gives no coordinates.

sources.title: West Berlin
sources.note: Whole dossier: sectors 1945, September 1948 separation, blockade, 1950 constitution, Wall, 1971 agreement, 479.9 km2, 3 October 1990.

sources.title: Allied-occupied Germany
sources.note: Berlin inside the Soviet zone but jointly occupied; opened for allied-occupied-germany and cited here only in notes.

sources.title: French Fourth Republic
sources.note: Opened by the eu-22-x reviewer for the end date of the Fourth Republic (5 October 1958).

notes: Requested as a counterpart by eu-22-a (the French sector). Start 1945 follows that dossier's occupation_start; the page treats 1945 as the division into sectors and September 1948 as the formal separation of the two city governments, so 1945-48 West Berlin is the Western sectors of a jointly governed city. Legal status 1949-90: not fully part of the Federal Republic (Western Allies kept formal authority; House of Representatives constitution of 4 August 1950; no vote in Bundestag elections); the federal-republic-of-germany author may record West Berlin as a client (vassal) of Bonn from 1949, which this dossier does not because the page calls the status ambiguous rather than dependent. The page was read to character 100000 of 100517; the Steinstücken exclave is not covered. Area: 479.9 km2, constant over the life; East Berlin, the Soviet sector, is not drawn separately (grid resolution) and belongs to the Soviet zone then the GDR.
